basis: D4 (T4), a person's seat at his next firm: every Heliogen Form 3 and 4 behind this row (July and August 2022) is filed by Krishna Kolluri, NeoTribe Ventures I, NeoTribe Partners I and NeoTribe Associates I, the shares held directly by NeoTribe Ventures I. Kolluri was an NEA general partner on the firm's archived people pages to 2016 and is the managing member of NeoTribe's general partner, his firm after NEA. No NEA entity is a reporting person, EDGAR full text finds no mention of New Enterprise Associates in any Heliogen filing (NeoTribe returns 50), and the firm has never listed Heliogen. The row came in only because Kolluri's own filer number was among NEA's filers.

The August 2019 S-1 holder table names RA Capital, TPG, Shin Nippon Biomedical, Wellington, Osage, CAM, Cormorant, Citadel and Eventide and no NEA fund, and EDGAR full text finds no mention of NEA in any Satsuma filing before March 2021. No earlier NEA private round. If Erik rules a PIPE a venture entry, the row enters at Growth in March 2021.

X1: the firm's own page gives 1993 as the year of NEA's first investment, and Dura became a publicly traded company in 1992 (In re Dura Pharmaceuticals Securities Litigation, S.D. Cal. 2006). Dura's 1997 proxy shows no NEA holder and no NEA director, EDGAR carries no NEA filing on Dura, and no source shows an NEA private round before the listing, so the 1993 purchase was into the listed company. The page's 'Early' label and its description (synthetic peptides for allergies and asthma, not Dura's respiratory products business) do not match the record, hence medium. If Erik rules a PIPE a venture entry, the row enters at Growth in 1993.

Not X1: NEA's position predates the listing. Premier Laser listed through its December 1994 IPO; its 1996 SB-2 lists an Amended and Restated Registration Rights Agreement of June 17, 1994 among the company, Onset Enterprise Associates, New Enterprise Associates IV and Franklin Capital Associates, the three venture firms that received $1.5M of secured notes in December 1993, exchanged them for convertible debentures in June 1994, and took 321,099 units for them at the IPO. NEA IV's 13G/A of February 1997 reports it has ceased to hold more than 5%. Flagged: the notes were issued in connection with Premier's purchase of Proclosure's laser technology, and the filings do not say whether they were new money or part of the price for Proclosure's assets; if the latter, D8 applies and Proclosure (not in base.json) is the member. Hence medium.

note: Fix pass F5: NEA IV entered before the December 1994 IPO, as one of three venture holders (with Onset Enterprise Associates and Franklin Capital) of $1.5M of secured notes issued in December 1993 with the Proclosure technology purchase, exchanged for convertible debentures in June 1994 and converted into IPO units (1996 SB-2). Not a listed purchase; no round is named, so the stage stays undetermined.

funding_rounds.round: Secured notes, exchanged for convertible debentures (June 1994), converted into IPO units (December 1994)

basis: D2 and D4, a partner's seat without fund money: pcOrder was a wholly owned Trilogy subsidiary until its February 1999 IPO. The IPO prospectus has Trilogy holding 98.3% before the offering and the rest in management options; Peter Barris, a director since June 17, 1998, is listed with no shares, and no NEA fund appears. The later ownership filings on pcOrder (1999-2000) are by Janus, FMR, Trilogy, West Highland and Gabelli, none by an NEA entity, and Trilogy took pcOrder private in its 2000 tender offer. No NEA fund held pcOrder; if the firm's money sat anywhere it was in Trilogy, which is not established and is not this row.

R1 control test: AMISYS (then American International Healthcare) was bought from AIG on May 26, 1994 for $10.0M cash through AIH Systems, Inc., which merged into it. All 4,800,000 Class A shares issued for the acquisition went to Greylock Equity (2,000,000), New Enterprise Associates VI and affiliates (2,000,000) and ABS Capital Partners (800,000), against 450,000 Class B shares, so the co-investor group acquired control of the whole company (May 1996 offering prospectus, Certain Transactions). A control acquisition, not a minority financing. Flagged: Greylock's row for the same company reads member, a cross-investor pair for rule 10.

D8, the Battery reverse-merger reading: in 2021 private Tempest merged into listed Millendo, which took the Tempest name. The merger S-4 shows NEA's stake on the Millendo side (1,766,407 shares held by New Enterprise Associates 15 and 372 by NEA Ventures 2015, 8.8% of Millendo), while Legacy Tempest's 5% holders are the Versant entities, F-Prime, Quan Venture Fund, LYFE Capital and LAV Regulus, and the Series B buyers the S-4 names include no NEA fund. Mike Raab, a Legacy Tempest director, holds personally and left NEA for Ardelyx by 2009. NEA's Tempest stock is Millendo stock carried through the merger, not an investment in Tempest; Millendo (row millendo, acquired) is the member.

The IPO registration's holder table names MPM Capital, Nomura Phase4 Ventures and OrbiMed and no NEA fund, and EDGAR full text finds no mention of New Enterprise Associates in any ARYx filing before November 2008. Not X1: Censtor was never listed. Its 1996 10-K reports no established public trading market for any class of its equity; it filed with the SEC only because its Series B preferred had 557 holders (registered under 12(g)). New Enterprise Associates V and Spectra Enterprise Associates (an NEA sleeve, D1) held 1,424,590 shares of Series A and Series B preferred, 5.86%, and NEA partner James A. Cole, Spectra's managing general partner, sat on the board from October 1992. A venture preferred position in a private company; NEA's 13G was filed under Rule 13d-1(d).

note: Fix pass F5, correcting the stage pass note: Censtor was never listed (1996 10-K: no established public trading market); NEA V and Spectra held Series A and Series B preferred, with NEA's James Cole on the board from October 1992. Censtor sold its manufacturing and R&D operations to Read-Rite in July 1996, kept only patent licensing, stopped filing after 1999 and had its registration revoked in 2011, so it is defunct.

basis: X1 and D8: the listed Graphix Zone, Inc. (Delaware) is the 1996 holding company that combined Graphix Zone (California) and StarPress. Graphix Zone had been listed since its June 1994 IPO, and NEA bought its common stock in a February 1996 private placement, a purchase into a listed company; the rest of NEA V's 900,114 shares (8.5% at end-1996) came from its 5,370,064 StarPress shares (16.06% of StarPress), exchanged at 0.14666 in the reorganization, which is merger consideration (1996 joint proxy statement and prospectus). No NEA private round in Graphix Zone before its listing. StarPress had itself acquired StarPress Multimedia, Inc., the likely venture position behind NEA's StarPress stock; neither is in base.json and that route is not established.

Not X1: NEA held Opta before its March 1992 IPO. Opta was incorporated in April 1991 from the food ingredients division of its predecessor Enzytech (an NEA company), and its 1997 proxy describes director Charles W. Newhall III, on the board since 1991, as a general partner of NEA Partners IV, the general partner of New Enterprise Associates IV, 'a venture capital partnership that is an investor in the Company'. NEA IV and NEA VI held 577,500 shares (5.26%) in 1997. NEA VI's larger block (472,500 shares) is not shown to predate the IPO, so the membership rests on NEA IV's pre-listing position. The filings read do not say whether NEA IV's shares came from a 1991 formation round or from Enzytech's division, hence medium.

note: Fix pass F5: NEA IV held Opta before the March 1992 IPO, Charles Newhall on the board from 1991, the year Opta was incorporated from Enzytech's food ingredients division (1997 proxy and 10-K); NEA VI's 472,500 shares are not shown to predate the listing. No round is named, so the stage stays undetermined.
